summary:
I measured at v34-frozen (sdkgen 89387a4f, tools e55846e), working in P/m20. Both clones were clean at the end.

- **H2:** documentation code shrank 2.06x (15,038 to 7,285 lines), 1.54x counting the forms and 1.20x counting the guard. The 2.06x is the first measured figure over 2x, and only on documentation code alone; it is 2.14x without the 259 lines of H5 machinery.
- **H1 prose:** by source, go is highest at 7.1%. By "printed by this language alone" against all twenty, go is highest at 14.8%, so no language is over 15% by either measure.
- **H1 purity:** 0 open findings in all twenty; 41 accepted with reasons.
- **H1 interface, re-counted from the code history:** 25 breaking provider-interface changes and 19 breaking forms-framework changes, 44 in all, against a limit of about 10. The record says about 25 to 27, and 31 to 33 with forms.
- **H1, caused by newly ported languages:** 0 for every port before the first wave. The first wave (perl, swift, ocaml, lua) caused 6 to 7 (2 or 3 provider, 4 forms). The second wave (the seven) caused 3 guard/forms changes and 1 changed shared sentence, with 0 changes to the provider types.
- **Sentences:** 385 distinct, 221 with a verdict and 164 without; 190 printed by one language only.
- **H3:** the checker over all 26 variations (alias-go2 included for the first time) exits 0, with nothing showing on NEW in any of the twenty. The per-language share is 2.8% to 5.6% by the brief's rule.
- **H5:** rebuilt from scratch, because the fixtures and builds were gone. Every row has the same verdict as before. F6 and F6b are now safe, and F11 is now caught both at release and by doctor. c5 is still open.

Highest by each measure:
- By source: go, 7.1% overall and 7.4% of its REFERENCE. At thirteen it was 7.2%, and 7.4% at v32.
- Alone: go, 14.8% overall. That is 17.0% against thirteen and 22.6% against nine; comparing against more languages lowers it.
- Notes: go, 6.9%.

No language is over 15% overall by either measure, and this is the first time the "alone" measure is under the line for go. By section, "alone" is still far over 15% in places: go's tutorial 33.5%, swift's tutorial 35.2%, php 18.1%, cpp 17.8%, and the root quick starts of c (93.5%), ts (93.3%) and perl (92.0%). These are shared result-style or lead-language sentences that one runtime's declared style selects (see sentences).

At the source, the shared templates hold 1,062 prose-literal words (980 at base33). Provider notes run from 0 to 45 words: go 45, lua 40, ocaml 31, zig and clojure 29, elixir 18, csharp 10, perl 9, rust 7, the rest 0. The seven add fact-table prose literals of 0 (java, scala) to 14 (kotlin) words.
purity:
RAN: `node tools/purity.js --providers ../sdkgen/ts/project/.sdk/src/cmp --lang <twenty> --root ../out/new --allow purity-allow` (logs/purity20.txt and .json). The same run without `--allow` gives the same counts: the tool reads its allow directory by default.

Open findings: 0 in all twenty.

Accepted: 41.
- The thirteen are exactly as at base33: ts 1, go 1, py 1, c 2, zig 1, clojure 4, rust 3, elixir 4, rb 2, perl 2, swift 2, ocaml 1, lua 1.
- The seven: js 1, php 2, csharp 1, java 8, kotlin 1, scala 2, cpp 1.

The reasons for the new ones:
- js and php: `exampleVarName` is called by no non-README component ("an example variable is not a name the code generator makes").
- php: a `require_once` path joined from `layout.dir` and `layout.module` ("not a name").
- csharp and cpp: a reserved-word list inside csVarName and cppVarName ("which a non-README component also calls: the code generator names things by this rule too").
- kotlin and scala: `.replace(/-sdk$/, '')` inside kotlinPackage and scalaPackage, for the same reason. scala also imports `scalaLit` and `scalaObjectLit` from utility_scala ("the scala generator's own literal table").
- java, 8 entries:
  - imports `javaMap` and `javaMapItems`, the generator's rule for a Map.of argument that leaves a NULL-typed member out;
  - imports `javaLit` from utility_java, the generator's one table of example literals;
  - 4 entries where purity misreads the constants JAVA_CORE and JAVA_ENTITY as functions (`.replace(/-sdk$/, '')` attributed to the wrong body), accepted with that explanation;
  - javaPackage, accepted as shared with the generator.

Judgement (read, not ran): java and scala are the first providers to import example-literal helpers from outside the printing helpers. Each is the language generator's own table, which the code generators call too, so no provider reads the model. H1's purity criterion (3 or more providers reading model facts) is not crossed.

interface_summary:
RAN and READ. I extracted every top-level type of example.ts, sdkdesc.ts, runtimeprose.ts and syntaxversion.ts at each commit from f21e6fe1 (the first four languages) to v34-frozen, and diffed consecutive versions (mine/typediff.js, logs/typediff.txt: 18 commits with type changes). I blamed every `throw` in the shared files (logs/throws.txt). For each commit I listed which Syntax_, Naming_, forms and guard-framework files it touched (logs/commit-touch.txt). I then read the commit messages and the diffs where needed.

A change counts as breaking when a provider, hook or forms file that worked before it must change to keep type-checking, generating or printing its own page. The forced lists come from the commits that followed each change.

**Totals:**
- Provider interface: 25 at v34-frozen (24 at v33-frozen). By round: v2 2, stage 3 1, v3 5, 3.1 1, 3.2 9, sentence fix 3, 3.3 3, H5's interface field 1. It is 24 if the testMock rename is merged with its requirement.
- Forms framework: 19 (16 up to 3.3). By round: v3 freeze 1, 3.1 4, 3.2 5, 3.3 6, 3.4 3. It is 17 if 3fa99737's three requirements count as one row.
- Together: 44 (42 on the merges). The limit is about 10. Changed shared sentences are not in these counts.

**Where I differ from the earlier reports** (appendix B and section 6.1: about 25 to 27, or 31 to 33 with forms, at 3.3; s6: 4 by new languages at 3.4 and 0 provider-type):
1. The four 3.1 guard tightenings are in no record's forms count: f2c4b95f, 39b8dc2b, a321926f and 1ac66964. Each forced every then-ported forms file; the commit series show it.
2. b8fd4fc2 (the reader marks members a runtime lacks) forced the c, scala, cpp and kotlin forms, and has no row.
3. Record row 33 bundles four guard commits (G6, G7, G8, G2-G5) and row 34 two. One row each gives 6 where the record has 2.
4. The testMock value rename 'model' to 'generated' (6a347c76) forced 7 providers and 18 forms, and has no row.
5. H5's `interface` field forced a line in all 20 providers. s6 calls the interface unchanged at '3.3' with 0 provider-type changes. The type allows omission, but an omitting provider is served as 3.2 and loses sentences, so I count 1.
6. Forced sets: `container` forced 4 providers, not 5; `read` required forced 7, not 8.
7. The record's v2 rows 4 and 5 are shared-only and touch no provider. Row 6, the naming hook, was optional with a generic fallback at v2 (additive by type); it became mandatory at 3.2 (b8a4a101), forcing 0. Row 1 predates the first commit and is not visible in history.
8. The record attributes only provider changes to wave 1. Brief7 states its guard items G1 to G8 had to fail "in each case the reviewers ran", so the 3.3 forms changes F11 to F14 were caused by wave 1 too.

H1's line is crossed on every reading.

h3:
RAN.
1. Copied P/h3fix/h3gen and issuecheck-h3fix.js into P/m20/h3. The generator stages an alias only for a clone inside its own workspace, so placed under P/m20 it could generate alias-go2. The integration had to skip that variation.
2. `node h3/h3gen/gen.js h3out/new sdkgen/ts`: 26/26 variations, 16 s. The clone was clean after the alias staging. The 21 variations shared with out/new are byte-identical to it, which confirms the copied out/new is v34-frozen's output.
3. `node h3/issuecheck-h3fix.js h3out --ported <twenty> --json logs/h3check20.json` (old = P/h3fix/h3out/old): exit 0, and 0 cells true on NEW for any of the twenty, across all 26 variations, the narrow checks, the broader 'any' variants and the post-attack ones (S22 any2, S13r2, bt2). lit, S13r and S13r2 have no OLD signal, as before.

New at twenty:
- N04, U06 and M04 (aliased go2 typing every field `any`) are now checked and clean on NEW. They were "X?" at the integration.
- N11 and M35 (a ts fence on js pages) are clean for js. js gets its fence from the provider's `fence` value, a syntax printer value.

Lines the seven ports added for a catalogued entry:
- S13 (testMock): 1 provider line each, 7 in all.
- Their forms citations were already present from the sentence round (65a16aef) in five of them. php and scala re-quoted theirs: 1 line each.
- js's S13 runtime fix (Config.fragment.js and Config.data.fragment.js, +3/-2 each) predates its port (b09502f1).
- No other catalogued entry needed a line in the seven. They carry no U44-style exception, and D26's open half (extend and utility rows need a per-language fact) is still done for no language.
- U44's two leftover exceptions remain in py.ts:93 and elixir.ts:97.

The ratio over the 36 in-scope entries at twenty. Each range runs from D26's open half counted for the proposal to it counted against:

| Reading | Per entry (of 36) | Per distinct defect (of 29) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| By the brief's rule (S13; D26) | 1/36 = 2.8% to 2/36 = 5.6% | 1/29 = 3.4% to 2/29 = 6.9% |
| Strict (+U44) | 2/36 = 5.6% to 3/36 = 8.3% | 6.9% to 10.3% |
| Strictest (+N04 U06 M04, M14: the type printers, now 20, and go's printer) | 6/36 = 16.7% to 7/36 = 19.4% | 4/29 = 13.8% to 5/29 = 17.2% |

These are unchanged from the record's thirteen-language figures. N11/M35, outside the 36, is now fixed for js through shared code; over 38 the brief's rule gives 2.6% to 5.3%.

Not re-done: the checker's 17 put-back attacks, and an independent reading of the sentences the catalogue round changed.
